output.population: Adults aged 20-65 years with type 2 diabetes diagnosed within 6 years, BMI 27-45 kg/m2, not receiving insulin, recruited from 49 primary-care practices in Scotland and Tyneside.
output.intervention: Primary-care weight-management program including withdrawal of antidiabetic and antihypertensive drugs, total diet replacement (825-853 kcal/day for 3-5 months), stepped food reintroduction, and structured weight-maintenance support.
output.outcome: Co-primary outcomes at 12 months: weight loss >=15 kg and diabetes remission defined as HbA1c <6.5% after at least 2 months off all antidiabetic medications.
output.effect: At 12 months, >=15 kg weight loss occurred in 24% of intervention participants and 0% of controls. Diabetes remission occurred in 46% versus 4% (odds ratio 19.7, 95% CI 7.8 to 49.8; P<0.0001). Mean body weight fell by 10.0 kg versus 1.0 kg; adjusted difference -8.8 kg (95% CI -10.3 to -7.3).
output.applicability_boundary: Applies to adults with relatively recent type 2 diabetes (within 6 years), BMI 27-45, and no insulin therapy, treated in UK primary care under this structured program.
output.source_span: Diabetes remission was achieved in 68 (46%) participants in the intervention group and six (4%) participants in the control group.

uncertainties: The trial was open-label and participants, carers, and outcome-data collectors were aware of allocation.
